Maria H: Heads up — we've been seeing a slow rising stream of CRC/checksum errors on ephemeral NVMe across multiple gnodes in us-east1 over the last 36h. Not a single catastrophic event, more like bit-rot drift on older drives.

infra-bot: alert: node=gnode-421 metric=nvme_crc_rate threshold=0.5% window=1h -- triggered

Maria H: This is starting to block GPU attaches when the provisioner tries to bind because the attach pipeline stalls on pending-deletes with underlying device read errors. Seen 12 attach failures in last 6h.

Raj P: Can you paste the smartctl/iostat snippets? Is this correlated to scrub/fstrim windows?

Maria H: paste: ```
# iostat -x 1 3
Device            r/s    w/s  rkB/s  wkB/s  await  %util
nvme0n1         120.4   10.2  5120  204.0   5.2   87.3
nvme1n1         0.12    0.03   0.8   0.2   0.5    0.1
```
and a dmesg excerpt: "nvme nvme0: I/O CRC error, metadata mismatch" repeated intermittently.

Cleo: Ugh. That pattern (high r/s on nvme0n1 and CRC errors) looks like hotstripe thrash + read retries. Are these nodes part of the janitor sweep wave currently running?

Maria H: Yes — janitor sweep cron windows started 2 nights ago after the overlayfs cold-start job. Sweep overlap + nightly scrub appears to be happening during peak GPU batch reclaim.

Aksh: If janitor is racing scrubs and heavy reads, we can trigger read amplification and expose latent blocks. Short-term mitigation: throttle janitor to 10% concurrency for us-east1 and disable deep-scrub on nodes with CRC > 0.1% until we get a plan.

Raj P: Agreed. Also we should mark suspect nodes as drain: avoid new GPU attaches, move workloads off, but keep them live for debugging. How many nodes are affected?

Maria H: Currently flagged 7 gnodes across 3 pools. All are preemptible but used for burst GPU attaches. If we drain them we lose ~320 GPUs available in the pool temporarily which will cause attach latency SLOs to degrade.

Cleo: Could we fallback to a compatible model variant or region routing (us-east2) for customer-facing critical attaches? We have routing policy variants for capacity fallback. Might be acceptable for short window.

Aksh: Yes — add a temporary routing policy: prefer us-east1, fallback to us-east2/us-west1 with cost-aware flag set. I'll open PR for routing change and the janitor throttle.

Aksh: PR refs: #4372 (routing fallback) and #4373 (janitor throttling script). ETA for deploy: 3 hours after approvals.

Maria H: For telemetry — I'm collecting checksums and SMART logs into a bucket (s3://redwood-debug/us-east1/nvme-bitrot/). If someone needs raw logs ping me and I'll share access.

Raj P: Long-term, we should tune scrub cadence based on drive age and live IOPS profile. Drives older than X months should switch to evening low-iops scrub window and aggressive read error thresholding so we don't escalate latent errors into provision failures. Add a task to infra backlog.

Cleo: Also propose a small change to the attach flow: add an early read-verify step that fails fast and returns a transient-degraded signal so the provisioner can pick a healthy node quickly instead of stalling. Low risk and should reduce attach tail latency.

infra-bot: incident-note: mitigation plan applied by Aksh — janitor concurrency reduced in us-east1, temporary routing fallback enabled.

Maria H: After throttling janitor we saw checksum alerts drop by ~65% in 20m. GPU attach tail improved from 120s -> 35s for the test batch. We'll keep monitors on for 6h and then decide on node drains.

Raj P: Great work. Please create a short postmortem note (2-3 bullets) and add the follow-ups: adjust scrub cadence, attach fast-fail, and lifecycle replacement schedule for affected drives.

Maria H: Will do — posting the short follow-ups in #postmortems once this stabilizes. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
